polity.en: Han-Zhao, Former and Later Qin, Western Wei, Northern Zhou
polity.zh: 前赵、前秦、后秦、西魏、北周

summary.en: Guanzhong capital of over ten dynasties including the Western Han, Sui and Tang, whose Chang'an was the eastern terminus of the Silk Road; renamed Xi'an by the Ming in 1369.
summary.zh: 关中形胜之地，西汉、隋、唐等十余朝建都于此，长安为丝绸之路东端起点；明洪武二年改称西安。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

note: Tang Chang'an and Han Chang'an occupy slightly different sites; one point is used.

story.en:
Chang'an, "Lasting Peace", was laid out by the Western Han south of the Wei River after 202 BCE, on a plain sheltered by the Qinling mountains and guarded by passes on every side. From here Zhang Qian set out for Central Asia, and silk caravans later took the road west from its markets.

In 582 the Sui built a new grid city, Daxing, just south-east of the Han ruins, and the Tang renamed it Chang'an. Its walls enclosed about 84 square kilometres, with 108 walled wards, an East and a West Market, Buddhist temples, Zoroastrian and Nestorian shrines, and perhaps a million people at its height in the eighth century. Japan copied its plan at Nara and Heian-kyō.

The city never recovered from the wars of the late Tang. In 904 Zhu Wen forced the court to Luoyang and pulled down its palaces. A much smaller town lived on as a regional seat, and in 1369 the Ming renamed it Xi'an, "Western Peace"; its present walls date from that dynasty. The terracotta army found nearby in 1974, the Big Wild Goose Pagoda and the Forest of Steles keep its imperial past in view.
story.zh:
长安意为“长治久安”。公元前202年后，西汉在渭河南岸营建长安城。这里南依秦岭，北临渭水，四面关隘环护。张骞由此出使西域，后来的丝路商队也从这里的市场启程西行。

582年，隋朝在汉长安故城东南另建棋盘式新城大兴城，唐朝改称长安。唐长安城墙内面积约八十四平方公里，有一百零八坊和东西两市，佛寺林立，还有祆祠和景教寺院，盛唐时人口或达百万。日本仿照它的布局营建了平城京和平安京。

唐末战乱使长安一蹶不振。904年朱温逼迫朝廷东迁洛阳，拆毁宫室。此后这里只是一座规模小得多的地方重镇，1369年明朝改名西安，今天的城墙即为明代所筑。1974年在附近发现的秦始皇陵兵马俑，以及大雁塔和碑林，让人得以窥见它昔日的帝都气象。

summary.en: Capital of four of the Five Dynasties and of the Northern Song, when Bianjing was among the largest cities in the world, as pictured in Along the River During the Qingming Festival; sacked by the Jin in 1127.
summary.zh: 五代中后梁、后晋、后汉、后周及北宋都城，北宋东京为当时世界大都会，《清明上河图》绘其繁华；1127年靖康之变陷落。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

note: Bianzhou dates from the Northern Zhou/Sui; the 781 boundary marks its becoming the Xuanwu circuit seat (simplified).

story.en:
Kaifeng rose with the canals. As Bianzhou it sat where the Bian channel of the Grand Canal brought southern grain north, and Zhu Wen, its military governor, made it the capital of his Later Liang in 907. Three of the four dynasties that followed also ruled from it, and in 960 Zhao Kuangyin founded the Song here.

Under the Northern Song the city, called Dongjing or Bianjing, may have held a million people. The ward walls and night curfews of Tang cities gave way to streets lined with shops, inns and entertainment quarters that stayed open late; Meng Yuanlao's memoir of the capital and Zhang Zeduan's Qingming scroll record that bustle. Because the flat plain offered no natural defence, the Song kept a huge standing army around it.

That weakness showed in 1126–27, when Jurchen armies besieged and sacked the city and carried off two emperors. Kaifeng then served as the Jin southern capital. Repeated Yellow River floods buried the Song city some eight metres under silt, beneath the remains of later cities; the worst, when the dykes were breached during Li Zicheng's siege of 1642, killed most of the inhabitants. A community of Chinese Jews lived here for centuries.
story.zh:
开封因运河而兴。唐代称汴州，地处大运河汴渠要冲，江南漕粮由此北运。宣武节度使朱温907年在此建立后梁；此后的四个朝代中，后晋、后汉、后周也都定都于此。960年，赵匡胤在这里建立宋朝。

北宋时称东京或汴京，人口或达百万。唐代城市的坊墙和宵禁被打破，街道两旁店铺、客栈和瓦子林立，夜市直到深夜；孟元老的《东京梦华录》和张择端的《清明上河图》都记录了这番繁华。开封地处平原，无险可守，宋朝只得在京城周围屯驻庞大的禁军。

1126至1127年，女真大军围攻并攻破开封，掳走徽、钦二帝，这一弱点暴露无遗。此后开封成为金朝的南京。黄河屡次泛滥，使宋代城市被深埋在地下约8米的泥沙之中，其上又叠压着后世的城池，形成“城摞城”的奇观；其中最惨烈的一次是1642年李自成围城期间黄河决堤，全城居民大多罹难。这里还曾有一个延续数百年的犹太人社区。

polity.en: Eastern Jin, Song, Qi, Liang, Chen

summary.en: Yangtze city that was the capital of the Six Dynasties as Jianye/Jiankang, of Southern Tang, the early Ming, the Taiping and the Republic of China; the Treaty of Nanjing was signed here in 1842.
summary.zh: 长江下游名城，六朝建业、建康，南唐金陵，明初应天，太平天国天京及中华民国首都皆在此；1842年《南京条约》签订于此。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

note: The ROC capital was in Beijing 1912–1927 and Chongqing 1937–1946; Nanjing is marked as capital for the period overall.

story.en:
Nanjing lies on the south bank of the Yangtze under the Purple Mountain, a site that an old saying likened to a coiling dragon and a crouching tiger. Sun Quan made it his capital, Jianye, in 229. As Jiankang it was the seat of the Eastern Jin and the four Southern Dynasties, a refuge for northern aristocrats and the centre of southern Buddhism and letters, until the Sui razed its palaces in 589.

It was a capital again under the Southern Tang and, from 1368, under Zhu Yuanzhang's Ming. His city wall, about 35 km long and built of bricks stamped with the names of their makers and overseers, still largely stands. After the Yongle Emperor moved to Beijing, Nanjing kept a secondary court.

Modern history returned to it again and again. The treaty that ended the First Opium War was signed on a British warship in the river in 1842; the Taiping made it their Heavenly Capital from 1853 to 1864; Sun Yat-sen was inaugurated here in 1912 and later buried on the Purple Mountain; and in December 1937 the Nationalist capital fell to Japan, followed by the massacre.
story.zh:
南京地处长江南岸，紫金山（钟山）雄踞城东，自古有“钟山龙蟠，石头虎踞”之说。229年孙权在此定都，称建业；此后作为建康，它先后是东晋和宋、齐、梁、陈四朝的都城，既是北方士族南渡的落脚之地，也是南方佛教与文学的中心，直到589年隋军平毁其宫室。

南唐和明初又在此建都。朱元璋修筑的京城城墙长约三十五公里，城砖上印有烧造工匠和督造官员的姓名，至今大部分保存完好。永乐帝迁都北京后，南京作为留都仍保留一套中央机构。

近代史上的重大事件一再在这里发生：1842年结束第一次鸦片战争的条约在江面的英国军舰上签订；1853至1864年太平天国以此为天京；1912年孙中山在此就任临时大总统，后来安葬于紫金山；1937年12月国民政府首都被日军攻陷，随即发生南京大屠杀。

summary.en: Frontier city of Ji and Youzhou that became a Liao secondary capital, the Jin Zhongdu and Kublai's Dadu, then the capital of the Ming from 1421, the Qing, the early Republic and the People's Republic.
summary.zh: 古称蓟、幽州，辽为南京，金建中都，元为大都；明永乐迁都后为明、清、北洋政府及中华人民共和国首都。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

story.en:
For most of its early history Beijing was a frontier town. As Ji and later Youzhou it guarded the north-east corner of the North China plain, where roads from Manchuria and the Mongolian steppe came through the mountain passes. That position made it valuable to northern conquerors: the Liao made it their Southern Capital in 938, and in 1153 the Jurchen Jin moved their main capital there as Zhongdu.

The Mongols took Zhongdu in 1215, and from 1267 Kublai Khan built a new city, Dadu, to its north-east; a canal later linked it to the Grand Canal. The Ming captured it in 1368 and called it Beiping, "the north pacified". The Yongle Emperor, who had been Prince of Yan here, rebuilt it as Beijing, "northern capital", with the Forbidden City at its centre and the Temple of Heaven to the south, and moved the court there in 1421.

The Qing kept the Ming city and added great gardens in the north-western suburbs. Except for 1928–49, when the Nationalists ruled from Nanjing and the city was again called Beiping, it has been China's capital ever since; on 1 October 1949 Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic from the Tiananmen gate.
story.zh:
北京早期长期是一座边城。它先称蓟，后称幽州，扼守华北平原东北角，来自东北和蒙古草原的道路都经由山口汇聚于此。正因如此，北方的征服者格外看重它：938年辽朝将其升为南京，1153年金朝迁都于此，称中都。

1215年蒙古攻破中都。1267年起，忽必烈在旧城东北营建大都，后来又开凿通惠河，与大运河相连。1368年明军攻占大都，改称北平。曾在此受封燕王的永乐帝将其重建为“北京”，以紫禁城为中心、南郊建天坛，并于1421年正式迁都。

清朝沿用明代城池，并在西北郊修建了规模宏大的皇家园林。除1928至1949年国民政府定都南京、北京改称北平之外，它一直是中国的首都；1949年10月1日，毛泽东在天安门城楼上宣告中华人民共和国中央人民政府成立。

polity.en: Former Liang, Later Liang, Northern Liang

polity.zh: 清 – 中华人民共和国

summary.en: Hexi Corridor city founded as Wuwei commandery by Emperor Wu of Han; as Guzang it was capital of several Liang states, and in 1247 the Sakya lama met the Mongol prince Köden here.
summary.zh: 汉武帝开河西置武威郡，古称姑臧、凉州，前凉、后凉、北凉建都于此；1247年萨迦班智达与阔端在此会盟。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

note: Some transitions are simplified.

polity.zh: 魏 – 清（荆州 / 襄州 / 襄阳府）

summary.en: Fortress on the Han River guarding the route between the Yangtze and the north; Zhuge Liang lived at nearby Longzhong, and the six-year Mongol siege that ended in 1273 opened the way to the Song heartland.
summary.zh: 汉水重镇，扼南北要冲；诸葛亮隐居城西隆中，宋元襄樊之战历时六年，1273年襄阳陷落，南宋门户洞开。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

note: The 1950–2010 name Xiangfan merged Xiangyang with Fancheng.

polity.zh: 中华民国 / 中华人民共和国

summary.en: River port at the Jialing–Yangtze confluence, known as Jiangzhou and Yuzhou, named Chongqing ("double celebration") in 1189; capital of Ming Xia and the Nationalist wartime capital during the war with Japan.
summary.zh: 嘉陵江与长江交汇处，古称江州、渝州，1189年宋光宗以“双重喜庆”升为重庆府；明夏都城，抗战时为国民政府陪都。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

name.zh: 上海特别市 / 上海市

summary.en: A fishing and cotton district of Huating county that became a market town under the Song and a county seat in 1292. Opened as a treaty port in 1843, it grew into China's greatest commercial city; the abbreviation Hu recalls the old Hudu shore.
summary.zh: 原为华亭县东北的渔业、棉业之地，宋代设上海镇，1292年设县。1843年开埠后发展为中国最大的工商业城市，简称"沪"即源于古称"沪渎"。

note: The date of the Shanghai market town is given variously as 1267 or earlier (Xianchun era).

summary.en: The landing place where the Grand Canal met the Hai River, garrisoned by the Jin as Zhigu. The Yongle Emperor named it Tianjin, 'the Son of Heaven's ford', in 1404. Opened to foreign trade in 1860, it became north China's chief port and the seat of the Zhili viceroys.
summary.zh: 大运河与海河交汇的码头，金代设直沽寨。1404年明成祖赐名"天津"，意为"天子渡津之地"。1860年开埠，成为华北第一大港和直隶总督驻地。

summary.en: Han Chinese settlers began farming the Taipei basin in 1709, and the river ports of Bangka and Twatutia grew on the tea trade. The Qing created Taipei Prefecture in 1875 and walled the city in 1884; it was the seat of Japanese colonial government and, from 1949, of the Republic of China.
summary.zh: 1709年汉人开始垦殖台北盆地，艋舺、大稻埕因茶叶贸易而兴。清廷1875年设台北府，1884年筑城；日据时期为台湾总督府所在地，1949年起为中华民国政府所在地。

summary.en: Taiwan's oldest city: the Dutch built Fort Zeelandia and Fort Provintia here, Koxinga made it the capital of his Zheng state, and it remained the island's administrative centre under the Qing until the capital moved north in the 1880s.
summary.zh: 台湾最古老的城市。荷兰人在此修筑热兰遮城和普罗民遮城，郑成功以此为明郑都城；清代长期为台湾府治，直到1880年代省会北移。

sources.title: Tonio Andrade, How Taiwan Became Chinese (2008)

polity.zh: 隋 / 唐 / 吴越 / 北宋

summary.en: Ancient capital of the state of Yue, the seat of Kuaiji commandery where Wang Xizhi held the Orchid Pavilion gathering. The Southern Song court stayed here in 1130–31 and renamed it after the reign title Shaoxing. Birthplace of Lu Xun and Qiu Jin.
summary.zh: 春秋越国故都，东汉以后为会稽郡治，王羲之在此举行兰亭雅集。1131年南宋朝廷驻跸越州，以年号改名绍兴。鲁迅、秋瑾的故乡。

polity.en: Sui / Tang / Southern Tang / Northern Song
polity.zh: 隋 / 唐 / 南唐 / 北宋

summary.en: Fortress on the south bank of the Yangtze where the Grand Canal crosses. As Jingkou it was Sun Quan's first base and the home of the Northern Garrison army of Eastern Jin; as Runzhou it was where Shen Kuo wrote his Dream Pool Essays.
summary.zh: 扼守长江与大运河交汇处的南岸重镇。古称京口，孙权曾在此建城，东晋北府兵驻扎于此；唐宋称润州，沈括在此写成《梦溪笔谈》。

name.zh: 临湘（长沙国 / 长沙郡治）

summary.en: Capital of the Han kingdom of Changsha, whose Mawangdui tombs preserved silk texts, and of the Ma family's Chu in the tenth century. Seat of the Yuelu Academy where Zhu Xi taught; the city was burned in 1938 and fought over three times during the war with Japan.
summary.zh: 西汉长沙国都城，马王堆汉墓出土大量帛书；五代时为马殷楚国都城。朱熹曾讲学于岳麓书院。1938年"文夕大火"焚城，抗战中三次长沙会战在此展开。

sources.title: 《长沙市志》第1卷 建置沿革

note: The Han kingdom of Changsha is not a separate polity in this dataset, so the Han entry is not flagged as a capital.

name.zh: 冶县 / 侯官（晋安郡治）

polity.zh: 吴越 / 宋 / 元 / 明 / 清

summary.en: Old capital of the Min Yue kingdom, renamed Fuzhou in 725 and the seat of the Min kingdom of Wang Shenzhi. Opened as a treaty port in 1842, it was the base of the Fuzhou Navy Yard, whose fleet the French destroyed at Mawei in 1884.
summary.zh: 闽越国故都，725年定名福州，五代时为王审知闽国都城。1842年开埠，1866年设福州船政局，1884年福建水师在马尾被法军击沉。

sources.title: 梁克家《淳熙三山志》卷1 地理类

note: Before 725 the names of the prefecture changed several times (Quanzhou, Minzhou); they are merged here.

summary.en: Part of Xin'an county under the Ming and Qing, the island was ceded to Britain in 1842, Kowloon in 1860, and the New Territories leased in 1898. Occupied by Japan in 1941–45, it returned to China in 1997 as a Special Administrative Region.
summary.zh: 明清时属新安县。1842年香港岛割让给英国，1860年割让九龙，1898年租借新界。1941至1945年被日本占领，1997年回归中国，成为特别行政区。

sources.title: Steve Tsang, A Modern History of Hong Kong (2004)

summary.en: A fishing harbour of Xiangshan county known as Haojing, where Portuguese traders settled from 1557 under Ming sufferance. The 1887 Treaty of Peking recognised Portuguese rule; Macau returned to China in 1999.
summary.zh: 香山县的渔港，古称濠镜澳，1557年起葡萄牙商人获准居留。1887年《中葡和好通商条约》承认葡萄牙管治；1999年回归中国。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Historic Centre of Macao

polity.zh: 清 / 中华民国 / 中华人民共和国

summary.en: Built as a Qing garrison town after the conquest of the Dzungars, it was named Dihua, 'to enlighten', in 1773, and became the capital of Xinjiang province in 1884. The Mongolian name Ürümqi, 'beautiful pasture', was restored in 1954.
summary.zh: 清朝平定准噶尔后在此筑城驻军，1773年定名迪化，1884年新疆建省后为省会。1954年恢复蒙古语旧称乌鲁木齐，意为"优美的牧场"。

sources.title: James A. Millward, Eurasian Crossroads: A History of Xinjiang (2007)
中文维基百科：乌鲁木齐市

note: The Tang town of Luntai stood nearby, but the name record begins with the Qing city.

polity.zh: 中华民国 / 中华人民共和国

summary.en: Walled city on the middle Yangtze, the key to the Three Kingdoms struggle that Guan Yu lost in 219. It was the capital of Emperor Yuan of Liang and the Western Liang, and of the tenth-century Jingnan kingdom; its Ming walls still stand.
summary.zh: 长江中游的重镇，三国时为兵家必争之地，219年关羽失荆州。南朝梁元帝和西梁（后梁）、五代荆南国都城于此；明代城墙保存至今。

polity.en: Yuan / Ming / Qing / Republic of China
polity.zh: 元 / 明 / 清 / 中华民国

summary.en: Founded by the Tangut ruler Li Deming in 1020 on the irrigated plain of the Yellow River, it was the Western Xia capital until the Mongols took it in 1227. The Yuan named the region Ningxia, 'pacified Xia'; the provincial capital was named Yinchuan in 1944 and became a city in 1945.
summary.zh: 1020年党项首领李德明在黄河灌区筑城，为西夏都城，1227年被蒙古攻破。元朝取"夏地安宁"之意称宁夏，1944年省城定名银川，1945年设市。
